<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par107" />{{GHGmargin-letter|107|q}}
(3) In dependent clauses after final conjunctions ({{GHGpar|165|b}}), as {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=7}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשְׁמְעוּ|translate=that they may not understand}}); {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲבוּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, 19, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=14}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫עַן אֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫עַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=51|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר יַעַ֫ן}}<ref>But {{GHGheb|text=יַעַ֫ן אֲשֶׁר}} in a causal sense (''because, since''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=2|verse=20}} (as {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=27}}) is followed by the perfect. On {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=24}} see above, {{GHGpar|74|g}}.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=12|verse=12}}, ''in order that''<ref>R.V. ''because he shall not see.''.]</ref>; {{GHGheb|text=לְבִלְתִּי|translate=that}}... ''not'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=14}}; also after {{GHGheb|text=פֶּן־|translate=that not, lest}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, &c.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=פֶּן־}} occurs with the perf. in a vivid presentment of the time when the fear is realized and the remedy comes too late. (In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=6}}, since a {{GHGterm|perfect consec.}} follows, read with Driver {{GHGheb|text=יִמְצָא}}.)</ref>; cf. also the instances introduced by {{GHGheb|text=וְלֹא}} in {{GHGpar|109|g}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=9|verse=6}} such an imperfect (or jussive? see the examples in {{GHGpar|109|f}}) is added to the expression of the command by an asyndeton, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=19}} to the principal clause simply by {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}: ''while they sought them food'' {{GHGheb|text=וְיָשִׁ֫יבוּ אֶת־נַפְשָׁם|translate=to refresh their souls}} (cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=26}}, ''it is good and let him hope'', i.e. ''that he should hope''); so after an interrogative clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=7}}. Finally also in a relative clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=32|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּדֶ֫רֶךְ־זוּ תֵלֵךְ|translate=in the way which thou shouldst go}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|r}}
(''b'') To express actions, &c., which are to be represented as possibly taking place or not taking place (sometimes corresponding to the ''potential'' of the classical languages, as also to our periphrases with ''can, may, should''<ref>By this, of course, is not meant that these finer distinctions were consciously present to the Hebrew mind. They are rather mere expedients for making intelligible to ourselves the full significance of the Semitic imperfect.</ref>). More particularly such imperfects are used—

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|s}}
(1) In a permissive sense, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=16}} ''of every tree of the garden'' ({{GHGheb|text=אָכֹל תֹּאכֵל}}) ''thou mayest freely eat'' (the opposite in verse {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=17|hidebook=completely|fullsizeverse=1}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=37|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=21|verse=3}}, 22, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=3}}. In the 1st pers. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=18|hidebook=1}} (''I may'', or ''can, tell''); in a negative sentence, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=5}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|t}}
(2) In interrogative sentences, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־יֹאמַר|translate=quis dixerit?}} Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=43|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=11|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹֽא־אֶרְחַץ בָּהֶם|translate=may I not wash in them?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=15|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=24|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=5}}. So especially in a question expressing surprise after {{GHGheb|text=אֵיךְ}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=9}} ''how then can I...?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=34|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=137|verse=4}}, and even with regard to some point of time in the past, looking forward from which an event might have been expected to take place, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲיָדוֹעַ נֵדַע|translate=could we in any wise know...?}} Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=33}} ({{GHGheb|text=יָמוּת|translate=was Abner to die as a fool}}, i.e. ''was he destined to die...?''), and so probably also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=31}} (''should he deal...?''). Very closely connected with this is the use of the imperfect—

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|u}}
(3) In a consecutive clause depending on an interrogative clause, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=11}}, ''who am I'' ({{GHGheb|text=כִּי אֵלֵךְ}}) ''that I should'' (''ought, could'') ''go?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, similarly after {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=2}}.<section end="par107" /><noinclude>
